name: Experiment name
description: Short and descriptive title [OECD GD 211]
alternative_definition: Descriptive full-text title [ToxTemp]

name: Study description
description: A description of why you did the experiment, what you hoped to see. This should be a 2-3 sentence description that would explain what this experiment is to someone other than you. [MIFlowCyt]
alternative_definition: Provide a summary of the assay features. E.g. “the effects of a chemical irritant on the opacity and permeability of a freshly isolated bovine cornea can be used to measure eye irritancy.” [OECD GD 211]

name: Date
description: Report the date of the first version of the method decription (day/month/year). Example: “5 August 2013” [OECD GD 211]

name: Version number
description: Indicate the date (day/month/year) of any update of the MD. The MD can be updated for a number of reasons such as additions of new information or corrections to the existing information. Summarise briefly which information has been updated.  [OECD GD 211]. For protocols, semantic versioning and fork tracking via dynamic repositories (e.g., protocols.io) are encouraged.
alternative_definition: Version number and date of deposition; Summary of introduced changes in comparison to previous version(s) [ToxTemp]

name: Organizations
description: Organization(s) performing the experiment. [MIFlowCyt]

name: Experimenter(s)
description: Name and email of contact person, Name of further persons involved [ToxTemp]. CRediT-style role attribution (conceptualisation, methodology, investigation, analysis, etc.) is encouraged.
synonyms: Corresponding person; Name and acronym of the test depositor
alternative_definition: The scientist that performed this experiment. [4DN] Primary researcher [MIFlowCyt] Names and contact details [OECD GD 211] Assay developer(s)/Laboratory and contact details [OECD GD 211]

name: Time point
description: Date and time (range) of the experiment [OECD GD 211]. Range form (start–end) is acceptable to capture the study time-frame.
synonyms: Study time-frame;study period start;study period end

name: Data access
description: Availability of data: e.g., open access or restricted data access

name: PubMed IDs
description: A numeric PubMed ID of a publication associated with this experiment or a comma-separated list on multiple numeric PubMed IDs if multiple publications are related to this experiment. [MIFlowCyt]

name: PMC IDs
description: A PMC publication identifier (i.e., PMCxxxxxxxx) of a publication associated with this experiment, or a comma-separated list of multiple PMC IDs if multiple publications are related to this experiment. [MIFlowCyt]

name: DOI
description: DOI stands for Digital Object Identifier. It is a unique ID to correspond to an electronic document such as an electronic journal article. Note, not all electronic journal articles have a DOI.  However, you may come across this ID on a journal article page, on a publisher's website, in a record in a database such as PubMed, or in a citation in a bibliography.  Some citation styles include the DOI at the end of the citation. [Health and science library]. Protocol DOIs (e.g., from protocols.io) are valid uses of this field for citing the procedure itself.

name: Reference(s) to main scientific papers
description: List of bibliographic references to papers that explain assay development [OECD GD 211]
alternative_definition: Availability of key publications [ToxTemp]

name: Test type
description: e.g., in vivo, or in vitro, ex vivo, in chemico, in silico

name: Endpoint(s)
description: Define the specific endpoint(s) of the test system that you use for toxicity testing (e.g., cytotoxicity, cell migration, etc.). Indicate whether cytotoxicity is the primary endpoint.What are secondary/further endpoints?Also describe here potential reference/normalization endpoints (e.g. cytotoxicity, protein content, housekeeping gene expression) that are used for normalization of the primary endpoint. [ToxTemp]
alternative_definition: The recorded observation coming from an in chemico method, an in vitro assay or an in vivo assay [OECD]

name: Availability  of  information
description: Indicate whether the assay is proprietary  or  non-proprietary  (to  what  extent  is  the  assay  method  transferable  or  contains proprietary  elements)  and  specify  (if  possible)  what  kind  of  information  about  the  assay  cannot  be disclosed  or  is  not  available  (e.g.,  chemical  reference  sets  (training  or  test  sets),  prediction  model). Example: “The assay is non-proprietary, but the training and test sets are not available”; “The model is proprietary, and the prediction model and associated data sets are confidential”; “Company XYZ’s in vitro model for sensitisation may be transferable but the prediction model is confidential”. Obviously ensuring scientific confidence in an assay is facilitated if all information is transparent and can be disclosed. [OECD GD 211]

name: Information about the throughput of the assay
description: Indicate the throughput of the assay to provide an indication of likely resource intensity e.g., low (manual assay, one chemical tested at a time), lowmoderate, moderate, moderate-high, high throughput (e.g., in 96 well-plate and higher), and qualify with e.g., approximate number of chemicals/concentrations per run. If appropriate indicate whether a manual assay could be run in a higher throughput mode. [OECD GD 211]

name: Status of the method
description: i)  Development  status:  Indicate  if  the  assay  is  still  under  development,  and  the  estimated  timeline  for completion as far as possible; ii) Known uses: summarise the current and/or past use of the assay by different laboratories; iii) Evaluation study: summarise the main conclusions or refer to individual protocol if available; iv)  Validation  study:  indicate  participation  in  a  formal  validation  study/studies  and  summarise  the conclusions and their outcomes or refer to the individual protocol if available; v)  Regulatory  use:  provide  details  of  any potential regulatory  application and  of  the toxicological hazard endpoint being addressed by the assay [OECD GD 211] If applicable: what is the status of the standardised assay, research, new method etc., is there an (S)OP? Reference to the SOP

name: Standards followed
description: Standards followed such as good cell culture practice [OECD GD 211] Information about qualifier, guideline, standards and deviations [OECD]
synonyms: GLP compliance statement;OECD TG alignment;OECD Test Guideline

name: Funding
description: List all funding sources (including grant number) and the role of the funder(s) in the study. [ARRIVE]
alternative_definition: You may reference funding sources for this experiment.  [MIFlowCyt]

name: Abbreviations and definitions
description: Used abbrevations and definitions of specific terminology

name: Supplementary Information
description: Name of the attached document(s) with remarks about content

name: Compound name
description: Used designation / name in the present work, standardized name of the nanomaterial (OECD)
synonyms: Material name;Nanomaterial;Compound designation;Substance;chemical name;formulation name;product name

name: CAS Registry Number
description: It is a unique numeric identifier, designates only one substance, has no chemical significance, represents a link to a wealth of information about a specific chemical substance [CAS REGISTRY and CAS Registry Number FAQs]

name: Sample source
description: Origin (who has produced/provided) of the sample

name: Hazards
description: Information about material safety. Physical hazards, e.g. nanoscale metal powders are very reactive and may have a high potential to explode (self-ignite). See also safety data sheet (SDS)

name: Structural formula
description: An empirical formula and molecular structure must be provided. [OECD]
alternative_definition: For the identification of chemical compounds

name: Procedure description
description: The suitability of the sample preparation methodology for the intended purpose. (OECD)
alternative_definition: Dispersion of as prepared or delivered NM in media used for biological experiments (DaNa)

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Cell name
description: Immortalized (naturally or engineered), genetically uniform tissue cells able to reproduce indefinitely in standard culture conditions. [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Type of test system
description: Category of the test system used (e.g. cell line, primary cells, tissue, bacteria, yeast), per IUCLID IntEff_Type. Carried by the cell-based test system's sampleType.

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Cell line origin
description: For each cell line, include in the Methods section a statement that specifies the source of the cell lines. Are any cell lines used in this paper listed in the database of commonly misidentified cell lines maintained by ICLAC (also available in NCBI Biosample)? [Nature]
synonyms: Cell line database; Cell line source

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Provider name
description: Name of vendor or lab (provider) that supplied the cell line [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Provider Catalog ID
description: ID or catalogue number or name assigned to the cell line by the vendor or provider [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Provider Batch ID
description: Vendor/Provider Batch ID number; Batch or lot number assigned to the cell line by the vendor or provider [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Organism
description: Organism of origin; a controlled vocabulary describing the organism from which the cell line was derived (e.g. Homo sapiens, Mus musculus, etc.)  [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Organ
description: Organ of origin; controlled terms describing the organ from which cell line is derived; (e.g. lung, mammary gland etc.)  [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Tissue
description: Tissue of origin; A controlled vocabulary describing the tissue from which the cell line was derived [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Cell type
description: A controlled vocabulary describing the cell type from which a cell line was derived, e.g. epithelial like, fibroblast-like, lymphoblast like, hematopoietic, mesenchymal, neural, etc. This provides information about cell morphology. Also sometimes referred to as cell morphology [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Cell type detail
description: Additional description of cell type (histology) that is not available in CL, but may be known from other sources like ATCC [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Growth properties
description: A controlled vocabulary describing the growth properties of the cell line (e.g. adherent, suspension) [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Donor sex
description: Describes sex of the organism from which the cell was obtained [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Donor age
description: The age of the donor [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Phenotype

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Genotype

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Donor ethnicity
description: For human cells, the ethnicity of the donor [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Donor health status
description: Controlled vocabulary describing the health status of the donor [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Disease
description: If the cell line came from a particular diseased tissue, the disease should be noted in terms of a controlled vocabulary (e.g. breast cancer, colon cancer, not diseased, etc.) [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Disease details
description: Additional description of a disease related to the cell line that may not be available in the disease ontology above [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Known mutations
description: Mutations inherent (from the donor) in the cell line, captured explicitly; e.g. if reference is not available [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Mutation citations
description: Mutations inherent in certain cell lines; from a reference [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Molecular features
description: Relevant molecular and morphological features of the Cell Line [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Genetic modification
description: This field specifies any stable constructs as well as any genetic modifications (mutations, translocations) introduced into this cell line (e.g. H2B-mCherry integrated at the AAVS1 Safe Harbor locus). Details of the procedures used to generate this line (e.g. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated transformation) should be described and appropriate citations provided in the Production Details field [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Recommended culture conditions
description: A description of the standard tissue culture conditions (media, supplements, culture dish treatment) used to maintain the cell line. Description of culture dish treatment conditions would include information about coating of culture dish with fibronectin, collagen, etc., prior to cell plating. If special culture vessels are required to grow the cells, these should also be mentioned, and details provided [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Related projects
description: Other projects in which the cell line has been studied / used; A controlled vocabulary describing other large-scale projects in which the cell line has been used (e.g. ENCODE, TCGA, ICBP, Epigenomics, etc.) [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Verification reference profile
description: Expected STR (reference) profile of the cell line based on provider information, if available [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Reference source
description: This field specifies a catalog entry or database record for this cell line at a cell type collection, if available, or an established external source [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Cell markers
description: A controlled vocabulary describing the markers used to isolate / identify the cell type [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Gonsome code
description: List of the sex chromosomes (gonosome) of the sample e.g. XX, XY, XXY [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Disease site onset
description: Site of disease onset in primary cell donor [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Disease age onset
description: Age of disease onset in primary cell donor (in years) [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Donor disease duration
description: Age of death of primary cell donor (in years) [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > General information
name: Cell relevant citations
description: List of references (with PMIDs) of relevance to cell line derivation, etc. [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > Custom fields
name: Culture conditions
description: A description of the culture conditions that were used and are suitable for this type of cell [LINCS]
alternative_definition: Precise cell culture method [Drasler]

section: Model characterization in vitro > Custom fields
name: Cell culturing material
description: Detailed description of the source and providers of the materials (cell culture plastic device)

section: Model characterization in vitro > Custom fields
name: Media preparation
description: Detailed description of the source and providers of the reagents

section: Model characterization in vitro > Custom fields
name: Cell seeding details
description: The number of cells seeded, percentage confluency at the start of an experiment, and time between seeding and experimentation should be reported for cell culture experiments. For experiments involving multiple cell types (e.g. co-culture, tumour spheroids), the number of non-target (e.g. healthy) cells and the number of target (e.g. diseased) cells should be reported. Ideally, however, the number of cells for each cell type present should be reported. [MIRIBEL]

section: Model characterization in vitro > Custom fields
name: Mycoplasma testing
description: Have the cell lines been tested for mycoplasma contamination? In this checklist, indicate on which page (or section and paragraph) the information can be found. [Nature]

section: Model characterization in vitro > Custom fields
name: Cell line authentication
description: Have the cell lines been authenticated? If so, by which method? [Nature]

section: Model characterization in vitro > Custom fields
name: Passage number
description: The number of times, if any that the cells have been re-plated and allowed to grow back to confluency or to some maximum density if using suspension cultures. [LINCS]

section: Model characterization in vitro > Custom fields
name: Cell growth
description: Description before and during the test performance [Drasler]

section: Model characterization in vitro > Custom fields
name: Morphology
description: Description before and during the test performance [Drasler]

section: Model characterization in vitro > Custom fields
name: Justification of biological model
description: If applicable, give brief summary and references for the prediction model; Consider the intended purpose of the prediction model [OECD GD 211]
alternative_definition: A justification of the selected cell culture. [Deagle]

section: Model characterization in vitro > Custom fields
name: Biological fluid characterization
description: For example, when investigating protein adsorption onto nanoparticles dispersed in blood serum, pertinent aspects of the blood serum should be characterised (e.g., protein concentrations and differences between donors used in study) [MIRIBEL]

name: Cell name
description: The name of the iPSCs that were differentiated [LINCS]

name: Cell type
description: Cell type of the differentiated cell. A cell type is a distinct morphological or functional form of cell. Examples are epithelial, glial etc. [LINCS]

name: Differentiation
description: Description before and during the test performance [Drasler]

name: Differentiation protocol
description: The protocol that was used to differentiate the cells [LINCS]

name: Transient modifications
description: Transient transfection or viral transduction [LINCS]

name: Days post differentiation
description: The number of days after the initiation of differentiation [LINCS]

name: Exposure
description: Route of administration / exposure e.g. aerosol, dispersion, oral gavage, intravenous

name: Vehicles
description: Dispersing agent

name: Incubation time
description: Incubation time, exposure time or duration and frequency of treatment

name: Readout frequency
description: Details on sampling

name: Dose
description: administered dose, the initially added dose

name: Dose settings
description: Number of doses/concentrations, testing range

name: Dose justification
description: Doses selected should be anchored by known human exposures; conversions from human exposures<-> in vitro exposures are suggested (via e.g. reverse dosimetry models). [Drasler]

name: Controls
description: Chemical positive and negative controls need to be included in each assay and the use of NM-based negative and positive controls is recommended. [Drasler]. For longitudinal control values across past runs (the historical-control dataset itself), see the dedicated `historical_control_data` row.
synonyms: Reference material;Positive and negative controls;acceptable control ranges;historical control data
alternative_definition: Reference materials are required as a benchmark control in toxicological studies in order to check the correct performance of the test involving positive and negative controls. [BfR]

name: Number of replicates
description: Number of technical and/or biological replicates. If replicates are not performed, provide a rationale (GD 34 p.40 §104, p.51 §149).

name: Specialized equipment needed
description: mendatory needed specialized equipment, e.g. electron microscope, specific sonicator or cell culture material etc.

name: Specific  licenses
description: e.g. permission to work with genetic modified organisms, license to use specific method/software

name: Sterilization
description: Removal of microbial contamination from nanoparticles. Important parameter for attributing the properties of the nanomaterial to toxic reactions that occur, including endotoxin removal.

name: Method(s)
description: Descritpion of the used in vitro method

name: Cellular model system
description: e.g 2D-, 3D-, Co-culture models. For complex models (organoids, spheroids, OoC, MPS), also capture dynamic physiological features such as fluid flow rates and mechanical stretching.
alternative_definition: NM response need to be assessed in multiple (at least three) different cell types and/or co-cultures. [Drasler]

name: Culture dimensions
description: e.g.  type of well, volume of added media, surface of the well

name: Exposure conditions
description: Physical conditions of the test environment maintained during test item administration: temperature, humidity, CO2 concentration, and the medium used (including its composition). Distinct from the steady-state maintenance conditions of the cell line itself, which are captured by `culture_conditions` and `recommended_culture_conditions` in the Biological Model module. The atomic parameters are also captured individually by their own GD 417 items (`incubation_temperature`, `incubation_humidity`, `co2_concentration`, `culture_medium`); for the medium, the component-level identity (sources, providers, supplements) lives in `media_preparation`. See GD 417 Table 2.1 p.21 and p.33 Sec 2.3.3 in vitro.
synonyms: experimental exposure conditions;in vitro exposure environment;culture medium during exposure;test medium

name: Units: mass or number concentration per cell
description: It is recommended that all the three-mass metrics are reported (mass, surface area and number) [Drasler]
alternative_definition: Dosimetry, delivered dose

name: Intracellular NM concentration
description: In the likelihood of intracellular NM alterations or dissolution, detection of intracellular NM concentration is recommended.  [Drasler]

name: Deposited dose on the cell surface
description: Deposited dose on the cell surface needs to be calculated (specified methods or models).  [Drasler]

name: Dosimetric conversions
description: Use of specific model systems e.g. Air-liquid interface (ALI) protocols for lung cell experiments may overcome the issue with suspension cultures by a direct deposition of a NM onto the lung cell surface. Use of ALI (and barrier protocols) avoids the need for many dosimetric conversions since most of the aerosolization systems can measure the deposited NM concentration on-line thus allowing to obtain a dose-related effect (Braakhuis et al., 2016) [Drasler]

name: Method(s)
description: Overview on analytical method(s) to assess test endpoint(s) [ToxTemp]
alternative_definition: Describe the response and its measurement [OECD GD 211]

name: Type of method
description: e.g. Quantitative or qualitative

name: Test method purpose
description: What is the claimed purpose and rationale for intended use of method, e.g. alternative to an existing method, screening, provision of novel information in regulatory decision-making, mechanistic information, adjunct test, replacement, etc.

name: Endpoint(s) of the test method
description: Response here makes reference to any biological effect, process or activity that can be measured [OECD GD 211]

name: Scientific principle of the method
description: Provide scientific rationale; Description of scientific principle; Biological/physiological basis and relevance; Mechanistic basis; Is anchor point an AOP? [OECD GD 211]
alternative_definition: Features of the in vitro test system that reflect the in vivo tissue [ToxTemp]

name: (Potential) linkage to AOPs
description: Link to KE (key event) or MIE (molecular initiating event)? Which AO might be modelled? If no AOP present, give link between mechanism the assay measures and resulting hazard endpoint [OECD GD 211]. Per the IUCLID OHT 201 schema, the AOP-aligned Process/Object/Action triplet (with GO/PR/CHEBI ontology annotations from the AOP Wiki, see Ives et al. 2017) is a structured population pattern for this row.

name: Method uses
description: Known uses: used in different laboratories? [OECD GD 211]

name: Applicability of test method
description: Potential solubility issues with the test system, and solutions proposed to address the issue [OECD GD 211]

name: Reagents
description: Add all reagents used in your experiment [MIFlowCyt]
alternative_definition: For mixtures, report the composition [OECD GD 211]

name: Kit
description: The kit used to perform this experiment, if applicable.  [MIFlowCyt]

name: Mechanistic validation
description: Indicate/summarize information on mechanistic validation, e.g. by omics approaches or by use of endpoint specific controls [ToxTemp]

name: Experiment variables
description: Experiment variables are attributes that differ between samples within an experiment due to pre-existing differences in sample states or due to experimental manipulation of the samples (e.g., smoker versus non-smoker, IL-2 treatment versus no treatment, knockout versus wild-type, or variable number of transplanted stem cells).  [MIFlowCyt]

name: Relation between assay-response and in vivo/biology/physiology
description: What is relation between assay-response and in vivo/biology/physiology? [OECD GD 211]
alternative_definition: Features of the test system that reflect the in vivo tissue [ToxTemp]

name: Robustness of the method
description: Reliability of the experimental results, Within-laboratory repeatability and reproducibility, Between laboratory transferability and reproducibility [OECD GD 211]. Historical control data referenced as evidence of robustness lives in the dedicated `historical_control_data` row.
synonyms: historical control data;intra-laboratory repeatability;intra-laboratory reproducibility;inter-laboratory reproducibility;inter-laboratory transferability;method transfer;ring test;inter-laboratory study;Applicability of test method
alternative_definition: Accurate and repeatable through validation [merged from the Exposure Information / Study design row 'Applicability of test method', a duplicate of this robustness/reliability concept].

name: Reference chemicals/chemical libraries, rationale for their selection and other available information
description: Are results for the reference chemicals (i.e. the “training set” chemicals used in the development and evaluation of the assay and its associated prediction model) free and publicly available in some form. If available, what is rationale for their selection. [OECD GD 211]

name: Metabolic capacity of the test system
description: Is the test system metabolically competent? Addition of an enzymatic fraction? [OECD GD 211]

name: Method randomization
description: If a method of randomization was used to determine how samples/animals were allocated to experimental groups and processed, describe it. For animal studies, include a statement about randomization even if no randomization was used. [Nature]

name: Blinding
description: If the investigator was blinded to the group allocation during the experiment and/or when assessing the outcome, state the extent of blinding. For animal studies, include a statement about blinding even if no blinding was done. [Nature]

name: Acceptance criteria for source cell population
description: Acceptance criteria assessed at different stages of test system and method, furthermore, assessing variability and troubleshooting. [ToxTemp]

name: Acceptance criteria for assessing test system at its start
description: List the criteria and the results

name: Acceptance criteria for the test system at the end of compound exposure
description: Criteria to accept or reject experimental data [OECD GD 211]

name: Raw data format
description: (file) Format in which original data are created, e.g. .tiff, .txt, any equipemt specific format, hand written notes etc.

name: Internal data storage
description: e.g. computer's internal hard drive, external hard drive, cloud, electronical or handwritten labbook, ...

name: Experimental system(s) used
description: Experimental test system extensively documented at different stages. [ToxTemp]

name: Equipment used, calibration program
description: Covers both routine maintenance and calibration; report frequency and most recent date for each.

name: Availability of internal standards
description: e.g. positive and negative controls

name: Limit of detection and limit of quantification, detection range
description: e.g. upper and lower detection range/limits

name: Cross-reference to related test methods
description: Related assays if known that may characterize the same key event [OECD GD 211]

name: Additional quality control experiments
description: If another experiment was performed for the purposes of establishing quality control standards, that experiment may be referenced. [MIFlowCyt]

name: Model number
description: The model number shall be sufficient if these uniquely specify the required instrument components. [MIFlowCyt]

name: Instrument Settings
description: e.g. microscope magnification, wavelength

name: Performance test
description: e.g. Sensitivity, Signal to noise ratio, Linearity [Deagle]

name: Software and version
description: Name of software, provider and version number

name: Data type
description: e.g. .czi, png, tiff, word, xls

name: Name
description: A user assigned name for this sample [4DN]

name: Description
description: A description of the sample that was imaged in this case. [4DN]

name: Preparation
description: e.g.  special sample preparation [4DN]

name: Fixation
description: Fixation protocol of the specimen, e.g. methanol for 20 min

name: Reagents
description: To show that antibodies were profiled for use in the system under study (assay and species), provide a citation, catalog number and/or clone number, supplementary information or reference to an antibody validation profile (e.g., Antibodypedia, 1DegreeBio). [Nature] Add all reagents used for sample preparation

name: Antibody
description: The analyte detector is often an antibody (e.g., anti-CD25) that specifically binds the analyte [MIFlowCyt]

name: Concentrations
description: Concentration of the used antibody solution [NanoS-QM]

name: Reactivity of the antibody
description: In a flow cytometry experiment, the analyte is often a cell surface protein e.g. CD25 [MIFlowCyt]

name: Host  of the antibody
description: Host of first antibody (e.g. made in mouse, rat, goat, rabbit) and secondary antibody (e.g. anti mouse, rat, goat, rabbit)

name: Clonality  of the antibody
description: e.g. Monoclonal, polyclonal

name: Fluorophores
description: e.g. Fluorescent dyes (fluorescent chemical compound that can re-emit light upon light excitation in certain wavelengths) in order to track its interaction with specific antigens. Antigen (e.g. GAPDH, or reactivity against certain subunit) [NanoS-QM]
alternative_definition: The reporter is typically a fluorochrome (e.g., FITC)  [MIFlowCyt]

name: Manufacturer / Source
description: Manufacturer and catalog number [MIFlowCyt]

name: Mounting method
description: Including description of mounting medium

name: Media type
description: Cells are alive, e.g. live cell imaging

name: Data analysis
description: Comment on the response value in terms of a boundary or range to provide a context for interpretation. [OECD GD 211]
synonyms: decision criteria;classification criteria;positive/negative/equivocal cutoffs;DIP;Data Interpretation Procedure

name: Explicit prediction model
description: Description of prediction model [OECD GD 211]

name: Raw data processing to summary data
description: Description how the data is calculated [OECD GD 211]

name: Raw data or distribution of values
description: Is the raw data or distribution of values underlying the reported results provided? [MIRIBEL]

name: Data Availability
description: E.g. external documents [OECD GD 211] Reference to additional files of relevance [ToxTemp]
alternative_definition: Please provide a Data Availability statement . Data availability statements should include, where applicable, accession codes, other unique identifiers and associated web links for publicly available datasets, and any conditions for access of non-publicly available datasets. Where figure source data are provided, statements confirming this should be included in data availability statements. Please refer the data availability and data citations policy of the "Nature" journal for detailed guidance on information that must be provided in this statement. [Nature]

name: Illustrations
description: Show us the spread: bar charts with error bars are commonly used to depict numerical data, but they can be misleading when sample sizes are small. Wherever possible, use graph types that include individual data points to directly show the spread of the data. [Nature Communications]

name: Curve fitting
description: Explanation of the curve fitting process [OECD GD 211]

name: Validation of statistics
description: Was cross-validation carried out? [OECD GD 211]

name: Details of data analysis
description: e.g. Image J cell counting

name: Software name and version for algorithm
description: Specify the name and the version of software applications (and date if relevant) used to derive the prediction model or to undertake the statistical processing. [OECD GD 211]

name: Statistical analysis
description: Provide details of the statistical methods used for each analysis, including software used. Describe any methods used to assess whether the data met the assumptions of the statistical approach, and what was done if the assumptions were not met. [ARRIVE]

name: Unit of analysis for each dataset
description: e.g. single animal, group of animals, single neuron [ARRIVE]
alternative_definition: Define your n numbers: just stating ‘n = 5’ is no longer sufficient—it must be clear what your n number refers to for each experiment. For example, did you do the experiment on five plants, on five tissue samples from the same plant, or did you run the same sample for analysis five times over? You should be able to justify your choice of sample size and statistical tests in the reporting summary. [Nature Communications]

name: Justification of statistical tests
description: For every figure, are statistical tests justified as appropriate? [Nature]

name: Estimation of variation
description: Is there an estimate of variation within each group of data? [Nature]
synonyms: coefficient of variation;standard deviation;measures of variability

name: Variance between groups
description: Is the variance similar between the groups that are being statistically compared? [Nature]

name: Methods to assess data
description: Describe any methods used to assess whether the data met the assumptions of the statistical approach. [ARRIVE]

name: Baseline data
description: For each experimental group, report relevant characteristics and health status of animals (e.g. weight, microbiological status, and drug or test naïve) prior to treatment or testing. (This information can often be tabulated). [ARRIVE]

name: Excluded data
description: Describe inclusion/exclusion criteria if samples or animals were excluded from the analysis. Were the criteria pre-established? [Nature]
alternative_definition: If any animals or data were not included in the analysis, explain why. [ARRIVE]

name: Outcomes and estimations
description: Report the results for each analysis carried out, with a measure of precision (e.g. standard error or confidence interval). [ARRIVE]. Per the IUCLID OHT 201 schema, the parameter_and_result flexible block (parameter name + numeric value + unit + remarks, repeatable) is a structured population pattern for reporting per-parameter results.

name: Adverse events
description: Give details of all important adverse events in each experimental group. [ARRIVE]

name: Protocol modification
description: Describe any modifications to the experimental protocols made to reduce adverse events. [ARRIVE]

name: Interpretation
description: Interpretation of data, observations

name: Study objectives and hypotheses
description: What was the initial aim and/or hypothesis of the study?

name: Primary and secondary experimental outcomes
description: e.g. cell death, molecular markers, behavioral changes [ARRIVE]

name: Current theory and other relevant studies in literature
description: What is the current theoretical background of this study, also taking other relevant studies into account?

name: Study limitations
description: Comment on the study limitations including any potential sources of bias, any limitations of the animal model, and the imprecision associated with the results. [ARRIVE] (Schulz et al. 2010)

name: Method limitations
description: Known technical limitations and strengths; Specification of any known technical limitations or strengths of running assay; The assay may not be technically applicable to certain types or class of chemicals. [OECD GD 211]

name: Limitations related to the data analysis
description: Explain the curve fitting process, the assumptions used to determine the goodness-of-fit and any limitations related to the data analysis. Indicate whether statistics was used (e.g. leave-one-out or other statistics). [OECD GD 211]

name: Implications of the experiment
description: Describe any implications of your experimental methods or findings, e.g. for the replacement, refinement or reduction (the 3Rs) of the use of animals in research. [ARRIVE] or for regulatory processes of the nanomaterial. For 3Rs assessment, structured elements per OECD GD 34 p.54-55 §163: databases searched, search strategy, search dates, and basis for animal numbers.

name: Generalizability
description: Comment on whether, and how, the findings of this study are likely to be translated to other species or systems, including any relevance to human biology. [ARRIVE]

name: Test method sponsor
description: Entity that has proposed a test method for incorporation into a Test Guideline, responsible for organising and providing all available information to the validation/review body.

name: Submitting party / national coordinator
description: Party through which the test method is submitted to OECD (Member country NC, EU/EC, BIAC industry association, or invited expert via NC).

name: Submission date
description: Date the test method submission package was provided for peer review / regulatory consideration.

name: Role in testing strategy / battery / tier
description: Indicates where and how the proposed test method might be included in the overall safety/hazard assessment process, including weight given relative to other tests in tier or battery.

name: Advantages over existing methods
description: Description of advantages of the new method (speed, cost, reduced animal use, etc.) over methods it replaces or complements.

name: Detailed test method protocol
description: Detailed, unambiguous step-by-step description of the test method including preparations, reagents, supplies, equipment, and criteria/procedures for generating and evaluating test data; provided as appendix to submission. Distinct from the `sops` row, which is for attaching the formal GLP SOP documents themselves.

name: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
description: Formal, written procedures describing in detail how specific routine and test-specific laboratory operations are performed; required by GLP. For attachment of formal versioned SOP documents (per GLP). The descriptive narrative of the test method belongs in `detailed_protocol`.

name: Standard data entry format
description: Standard format for data entry to be used by all participating laboratories, with clear directions on how to report data and related information.

name: Dose-response relationship analysis
description: Methods used to explore the dose-response relationship.

name: Chemical class
description: Chemical class to which each test substance belongs.

name: Product class
description: Product class to which each test substance belongs.

name: Purity
description: Purity of each test substance; chemicals should be of highest available purity or of known composition.

name: Physical and chemical characteristics
description: Physico-chemical data such as pH, volatility, stability, solubility, chemical reactivity, provided for each test chemical. Includes nanomaterial-specific facets where applicable: particle size and size distribution, shape, surface area, surface charge, and surface treatment.

name: Weight or volume of sample dispatched
description: Weight or volume of the sample of test chemical dispatched to the participating laboratory.

name: Storage instructions / conditions
description: Storage instructions for the test chemical; chemicals should be stable under defined storage conditions for at least the duration of the validation study.

name: Stability of test substance in test medium
description: Stability of each test substance under the test conditions and test medium. Where degradation occurs, identify and quantify degradation products.

name: Sorption/bioavailability considerations
description: Sorption to plastic plates, PDMS absorption, or binding to albumin/serum can reduce bioavailability; such physicochemical-driven exposure effects should be evaluated (e.g., with computational models).

name: Batch / lot number
description: All laboratories should use, to the extent possible, the same batch of a test chemical; lot-to-lot consistency should be described.
iri_label: Lot or Batch Number Production Identifier

name: Mixture constituents and relative concentrations
description: In the case of mixtures, the constituents and their relative concentrations should be stated whenever possible.

name: Source of in vivo / reference test data
description: Source of the in vivo reference test method data (literature citation for published information, laboratory study director, year generated for unpublished data).

name: Reference test method protocol description
description: Description of the protocol(s) employed to generate the in vivo reference test method or human data, including any modifications and their potential impact.

name: Quality of in vivo reference test data (GLP)
description: Description of the quality of the in vivo reference data, including extent of GLP compliance and use of coded test chemicals.

name: Comparative test/reference data table
description: Table of test method results versus reference test method results (quantitative and categorical), for each test substance (Table 4 template).

name: Accuracy
description: Closeness of agreement between test method results and accepted reference values; measure of test method performance. Sub-metrics: sensitivity (proportion of positives correctly classified), specificity (proportion of negatives correctly classified), positive predictivity, negative predictivity, false positive rate, false negative rate. Prevalence (proportion of positives/negatives in the test set) provides context for interpreting these metrics. See GD 34 Annex I, p.54 §158.

name: Quality assurance / quality control procedures
description: QA/QC procedures to which the original data and derived values are subjected; management process for adherence to laboratory testing standards.

name: Historical control data
description: Longitudinal dataset of control values (negative, positive, vehicle) from previous runs of the test method, used as evidence of method reliability and to define acceptable ranges for current experiments. Typically attached as a CSV/Excel table, a control chart, or summary statistics (mean, SD, CV). Distinct from `controls` (per-experiment control descriptions) and `robustness_of_the_method` (the reliability narrative); historical control data is the underlying dataset that feeds both. See GD 417 p.24 Sec 2.2.1.

name: Cost and time of conducting the test
description: Cost and time involved in conducting a study using the proposed test method, compared to reference test method(s).

name: Nanomaterial dispersion/aggregation measures
description: For nanomaterial studies, particle size, shape and surface charge must be considered and appropriate measures taken to ensure homogeneous dispersion and avoid particle aggregation.

name: Analytical verification of nominal concentrations
description: Ideally, nominal concentrations should be analytically verified; for chemically unstable substances more frequent analyses may be needed.

name: Effective (bioavailable) concentration measurement
description: To determine bioavailability during the experiment, the effective concentration of the test item should be measured to aid interpretation of results.

name: Analytical verification of test item identity
description: Analytical verification of the test item should be conducted at study initiation and termination (and during, for longer studies) to verify substance identity and stability.

name: Sample size
description: Number of independent experimental units used for statistical analysis (the 'n' that determines degrees of freedom and underpins statistical power). For in vitro studies, this is typically the number of biological replicates rather than technical replicates (pseudoreplicates). Pairs with `statistical_power`: power analysis requires sample size as input, and sample size is what power analysis prescribes. Distinct from `number_of_replicates` (generic replicate count) and `unit_of_analysis_for_each_dataset` (the type of unit). See GD 417 p.22 Table 2.1; p.29-30 Sec 2.3.1.

name: Statistical power
description: Statistical power considerations, including sample size overall and across subgroups, should be addressed in the design.

name: Access to analysis code
description: Access to code used for data analysis / modelling (noted for computational studies, applicable to in vitro bioinformatics workflows).

name: Machine-readable results tables
description: Reporting of main results in machine-readable tables comprising relevant endpoints and statistical parameters facilitates interpretation and data extraction.

section: Model characterization in vitro > Custom fields
name: Scaffolds / matrices for 3D models
description: For complex in vitro models (organoids, spheroids, OoC, MPS, 3D bioprinting), matrices or scaffolds used (e.g., Matrigel, collagen, fibrin gel) should be reported.

section: Model characterization in vitro > Custom fields
name: Device manufacturing materials
description: For MPS/OoC devices, the materials used for manufacturing (e.g., PDMS or other polymers) should be reported, as they can influence compound absorption.

name: Peer review status
description: Peer review is often a prerequisite for regulatory consideration of research data; reporting of peer-review status supports reliability assessment.

name: Pre-registration of protocol
description: Pre-registration of protocols (e.g., in study registries such as clinical trial registries or animal study registries) reduces publication bias and increases transparency.
